diagnosis.finding: Watchdog performs repeated global identity snapshots with timeout 0.5 seconds. Timeout raises through owned into the watchdog exception path immediately, independently of the absolute deadline. It records first failure 124 and performs bound-group/direct-child fallback cleanup. The recorded failure at 07:06:16.407952Z is not expiry of the 07:09:02.787484Z whole deadline.

First failure remains watchdog/124 despite the direct guard command later returning 1 at 07:06:16.731159Z. Watchdog exits after its own failed terminal finalisation and can end the main thread before main cleanup writes its process audit. This explains missing final audit without treating absence as cleanup success.

Guard spawns detached worker, records its group, installs TERM handler calling killTree then finish. killTree tries group SIGKILL plus currently discoverable descendant PIDs; finish writes end and releases its own lock without verifying every target exit. Actual guard end reports stopped by SIGTERM at 07:06:16.664Z, sampled peak 322 MB, three observed processes, 6.7 seconds. This is actual handler-path evidence, not proof all signals succeeded.

Underlying reason the global ps exceeded 0.5 seconds is not established. Later successful snapshots with that same timeout do not disprove the transient failure or justify increasing it. No CPU, memory or build defect is inferred.

owned_universe.scope: Each command starts a new session and is registered immediately in children plus roots; birth is filled after ps. Git archive command completed and was removed. Guard PID 55177 was the active registered direct child and later reaped with command exit 1. Outer PID and historical git PID/birth are not durably enumerated in these receipts.

Validated worker PID/PGID 55188, UTC/C birth, actual observed parent 55177, context hash and nonce are retained before ACK. job_groups and roots bind its group independently of guard lifetime. Worker build subprocess has no new-session/detached option and inherits group 55188; its PID is not separately recorded.

Outer discovers matching retained births, descendants of owned parents and members of bound groups. Guard discovers worker descendants plus group members. Inspected esbuild service spawn has no detached option and normally inherits the build group. Guard ps/sysctl/footprint helpers are separate subprocesses under the guard rather than the worker group. No complete historical PID/birth ledger of helpers or all transitive build descendants was retained. Sampled peak three is not a census or proof no other process existed.
